answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may place jobs, and slash that stake when an independent audit proves fraud, such as claiming payment for duplicated work. A reputation score can then grow only through completed jobs with distinct counterparties, so minting many names does not instantly create trust. The ember of a small account may echo across a sonnet of fake profiles, but each still needs capital and useful work; the attacker pays for every identity and risks losing the stake.
